title: The Great Pizza Debate
summary: New York or Chicago? Detroit or New Haven? Weigh in on the great pizza debate with our guide to 20+ regional pizza styles, shipped nationwide.

## New York vs. Chicago vs. Detroit & More: Which Pizza Style Wins?


Few food fights run hotter than pizza. New Yorkers swear by the fold, Chicagoans defend deep-dish (and quietly eat tavern-style), Detroit claims the crispiest edges, and New Haven insists its apizza isn’t pizza at all. With more than 20 regional styles across America, here’s the case for each one, plus where to order the most iconic versions shipped nationwide on Goldbelly, so you can be the judge.


**Settle the debate for less:** Pizzas are on sale all October long for National Pizza Month, with up to 30% off in the Pizza Month Sale.


[Pizza Month Sale](https://www.goldbelly.com/collections/pizza-sale)


## **New York Style: The Quintessential Slice**


When you think of pizza, this is probably what you picture.[New York-style pizza](https://www.goldbelly.com/foods/new-york-style-pizza) means big, thin-crusted slices with a crisp-chewy bottom, cut wide enough to fold in half and eat on the go. For a virtual trip to a New York street corner, look no further than these iconic purveyors:


- [Di Fara Pizza](https://www.goldbelly.com/restaurants/di-fara-pizza)
- [Lombardi’s](https://www.goldbelly.com/restaurants/lombardis-pizza) ( **Read More:[America’s First Pizzeria](https://blog.goldbelly.com/lombardis-pizza-shipping-nationwide/)**[!](https://blog.goldbelly.com/what-is-new-york-style-pizza/) )
- [John’s of Bleecker Street](https://www.goldbelly.com/restaurants/johns-of-bleecker-street)
- [Joe & Pat’s](https://www.goldbelly.com/restaurants/joe-and-pats-pizzeria)
- [Juliana’s](https://www.goldbelly.com/restaurants/julianas-pizza)
- [Prince Street Pizza](https://www.goldbelly.com/restaurants/prince-street-pizza) , home of the SoHo square
- [Artichoke Basille’s](https://www.goldbelly.com/restaurants/artichoke-basilles-pizza)
- [Table 87](https://www.goldbelly.com/restaurants/table-87)
- [Tony Boloney’s](https://www.goldbelly.com/restaurants/tony-boloneys)
- [Mother Kelly’s](https://www.goldbelly.com/restaurants/mother-kellys)


**The case for it:** It’s the slice that defined American pizza, and the only one you can fold and eat on the walk.


## **Sicilian & Grandma Style: New York’s Square Pies**


New York’s pizza story doesn’t end with the round slice.[Sicilian pizza](https://www.goldbelly.com/foods/sicilianpizza) is baked in a rectangular pan with a thick, airy, focaccia-like crust. Brooklyn’s[L&B Spumoni Gardens](https://www.goldbelly.com/restaurants/lb-spumoni-gardens) has been famous for its saucy Sicilian squares since 1939, and Fort Worth’s[Zoli’s NY Pizza](https://www.goldbelly.com/restaurants/zolis-ny-pizza) brings the style to Texas.


[Grandma pizza](https://www.goldbelly.com/foods/grandmapizza) is its thinner Long Island cousin: dough pressed into an oiled pan, topped with cheese, and finished with dollops of tomato sauce.[Umberto’s Pizzeria](https://www.goldbelly.com/restaurants/umbertos-pizzeria) in New Hyde Park is often credited with popularizing it. Try it from Umberto’s,[Washington Squares](https://www.goldbelly.com/restaurants/washington-squares) , or[Loring Place](https://www.goldbelly.com/restaurants/loring-place) .


**The case for it:** All the crispy, golden corner pieces you could want, in one pan.


**Read More:**[What Is Grandma Pizza? The NY Square Slice Explained](https://blog.goldbelly.com/what-is-grandma-pizza/)


## **Chicago Style: Not Just Deep-Dish**


The Windy City is synonymous with[deep-dish pizza](https://www.goldbelly.com/foods/chicago-deep-dish-pizza) : a high-edged, buttery crust filled with gooey cheese, ample toppings, and chunky tomato sauce on top. These are some of the most legendary deep-dish pizzerias:


- [Lou Malnati’s](https://www.goldbelly.com/restaurants/lou-malnatis-pizzeria)
- [Gino’s East](https://www.goldbelly.com/restaurants/ginos-east)
- [Giordano’s](https://www.goldbelly.com/restaurants/giordanos-pizza)
- [Pequod’s](https://www.goldbelly.com/restaurants/pequods-pizza) , famous for its caramelized cheese crust


Chicagoans will tell you the pizza they actually eat most is[Chicago thin-crust](https://www.goldbelly.com/foods/chicago-thin-crust-pizza) . Its crust is almost cracker-thin, and it’s cut into squares, “tavern-style.” For an authentic taste, look no further than[Lou Malnati’s](https://www.goldbelly.com/restaurants/lou-malnatis-pizzeria) ,[Labriola](https://www.goldbelly.com/restaurants/labriola-chicago) ,[Connie’s](https://www.goldbelly.com/restaurants/connies-pizza) , and[Candlelite](https://www.goldbelly.com/restaurants/candlelite-chicago-pizza) .


Then there’s[stuffed pizza](https://www.goldbelly.com/foods/stuffedpizza) , deep-dish’s even taller sibling, with a second layer of dough sealing in the cheese and toppings beneath the sauce.[Nancy’s Pizza](https://www.goldbelly.com/restaurants/nancys-pizza) has been a stuffed-pizza standard-bearer since the 1970s.


**The case for it:** Three distinct styles from one city. No other pizza town can match that range.


**Read More:**[What is Chicago-Style Deep-Dish Pizza?](https://blog.goldbelly.com/what-is-chicago-style-deep-dish-pizza/)


## **Detroit Style: Thick, Crisp & Chewy**


Invented in the mid-1900s,[Detroit-style pizza](https://www.goldbelly.com/foods/detroit-style-pizza) was originally baked in rectangular steel trays used to hold automotive parts. These square pies have an airy, chewy crust with a crisp bottom, cheese baked all the way to the edges, and “racing stripes” of tomato sauce on top. Bring a taste of Detroit home with[Buddy’s Pizza](https://www.goldbelly.com/restaurants/buddys-pizza) , where the style was invented, and[Detroit Style Pizza Co.](https://www.goldbelly.com/restaurants/detroit-pizza-company) The style has gotten so popular that Brooklyn’s[Emmy Squared](https://www.goldbelly.com/restaurants/emmy-squared) built a following on Detroit squares with a New York twist.


**The case for it:** Those caramelized, crispy cheese edges. Every piece is a corner piece.


## **New Haven Style: Don’t Call it Pizza!**


In New Haven, Connecticut, it’s called[apizza](https://www.goldbelly.com/foods/new-haven-pizza) (pronounced “ah-BEETZ,” from an old Neapolitan dialect). It may resemble New York-style pizza, but it’s totally different: coal-fired, slightly charred, chewy, and a little oblong. One bite and you’ll be hooked. Crowds line up for the state’s most iconic pizzerias, including:


- [Sally’s Apizza](https://www.goldbelly.com/restaurants/sallys-apizza)
- [Zuppardi’s Apizza](https://www.goldbelly.com/restaurants/zuppardis-apizza)
- [Carmine’s Pizzas](https://www.goldbelly.com/restaurants/carmines-pizza-llc)
- [Piece Pizzeria](https://www.goldbelly.com/restaurants/piece-pizzeria) , a New Haven-style pizzeria in Chicago


**The case for it:** Coal-fired char and a chewy crust that devotees happily wait in line for.


**Read More:[What is “Apizza,” New Haven Style Pizza?](https://blog.goldbelly.com/what-is-new-haven-style-pizza/)**


## **Neapolitan Style: Straight Outta Naples**


Naples obviously isn’t in America, but we’d be remiss to leave the birthplace of pizza off this list. Traditional[Neapolitan pizza](https://www.goldbelly.com/foods/neapolitan-pizza) has a soft, puffy, leopard-spotted crust surrounding tomato sauce, fresh mozzarella, and few other toppings, with a slightly soupy center. It’s the pizza every other style descends from, and some of America’s best versions come from:


- San Francisco’s[Pizzeria Delfina](https://www.goldbelly.com/restaurants/pizzeria-delfina)
- Phoenix’s[Pizzeria Bianco](https://www.goldbelly.com/restaurants/pizzeria-bianco)
- LA’s[Pizzana](https://www.goldbelly.com/restaurants/pizzana)
- New York’s[Motorino](https://www.goldbelly.com/restaurants/motorino-pizzeria)


**The case for it:** It’s the original. Every other style on this list starts here.


## **Roman Style: Pizza by the Slab**


Rome’s answer to Naples is[Roman-style pizza](https://www.goldbelly.com/foods/roman-style-pizza) , especially *pizza al taglio* , which means “by the cut.” It’s baked in long rectangular pans with a light, crackly, open-crumb crust, then sliced to order with toppings that change with the seasons. Get the real deal from[Bonci Pizza](https://www.goldbelly.com/restaurants/bonci-pizza) , the famous Roman pizzeria that brought its slabs to Chicago.


**The case for it:** A crust so light and crackly it practically shatters.


## **Colorado Style: Thick-Crusted “Mountain Pies”**


[Colorado-style pizza](https://www.goldbelly.com/foods/colorado-style-pizza) is big, bold, and unapologetic. These pies are heavy, doughy, and loaded with toppings, often ringed by a braided crust meant for a drizzle of honey. One is enough to feed a family. Try this lesser-known regional style from Idaho Springs’[Beau Jo’s](https://www.goldbelly.com/restaurants/beau-jos-pizza) and Fort Collins’[Panhandler’s](https://www.goldbelly.com/restaurants/panhandlers-pizza) .


**The case for it:** It’s the only pizza with dessert built in: just add honey to the crust.


## **Philadelphia Style: A Different Type of Tomato Pie**


Visit any of Philly’s classic old Italian bakeries and you’ll find a close relative of pizza that’s rarely seen outside the City of Brotherly Love: the[tomato pie](https://www.goldbelly.com/foods/tomato-pie) . These pies are light, airy, and crisp, served at room temperature, and topped with a sweet tomato sauce and a sprinkling of Romano instead of mozzarella.[Corropolese Bakery](https://www.goldbelly.com/restaurants/corropolese-italian-bakery-and-deli) has been making one of the city’s most iconic tomato pies since 1924, and[Iannelli’s Bakery](https://www.goldbelly.com/restaurants/iannellis-bakery) has been a local landmark since 1910.


**The case for it:** Pizza that’s meant to be eaten at room temperature, so no reheating required.


## **New Jersey Style: Tomato Pies on the Shore**


Head to the Jersey Shore and you’ll find a style that resembles its cousin to the north but is a style all its own: the Jersey tomato pie. These pies are big and cheesy, sold by the slice along the boardwalk, and best identified by their swirl of tomato sauce on top. To transport yourself to the shore, order from Seaside Heights’[Maruca’s Tomato Pies](https://www.goldbelly.com/restaurants/marucas-tomato-pies) , the tomato pie gold standard since 1950.


**The case for it:** That sauce swirl is a work of art, and every bite tastes like summer on the boardwalk.


## **Bar Pie: Thin, Crispy & Built for a Pint**


[Bar pie](https://www.goldbelly.com/foods/bar-pie) is a tavern classic in two corners of the Northeast: New Jersey and Massachusetts’ South Shore. These personal-size pies have an ultra-thin, crispy crust, with cheese baked right up to the edge of the pan until it caramelizes. Get a taste from New Jersey’s[The Columbia Inn](https://www.goldbelly.com/restaurants/the-columbia-inn) and Massachusetts’[Cape Cod Cafe](https://www.goldbelly.com/restaurants/cape-cod-cafe-pizza) .


**The case for it:** Crispy, cheesy edge to edge, and sized so you never have to share.


## **St. Louis Style: Square Beyond Compare**


Meet me in St. Louis for some insanely good pizza.[St. Louis-style pizza](https://www.goldbelly.com/foods/st-louis-style-pizza) has a cracker-thin, yeast-free crust topped with an oregano-heavy tomato sauce and Provel, a white processed cheese that melts into gooey deliciousness, all cut into squares. Picture-perfect St. Louis pizza comes from the city’s renowned[Imo’s Pizza](https://www.goldbelly.com/restaurants/imos-pizza) , going strong for more than 60 years.


**The case for it:** Provel. Love it or hate it, no other pizza tastes like this.


## **Old Forge Style, PA: The Dark Horse**


It takes some nerve to call yourself “The Pizza Capital of the World,” but that’s exactly what the tiny town of Old Forge, Pennsylvania, has done.[Old Forge pizza](https://www.goldbelly.com/foods/old-forge-pizza) has a thick crust that’s light and airy, topped with plenty of cheese and sauce. You can try it without a trip to Lackawanna County by ordering from the town’s renowned[Arcaro & Genell](https://www.goldbelly.com/restaurants/arcaro-and-genell) .


**The case for it:** It’s the self-proclaimed pizza capital of the world. Bold claims deserve a taste.


## **Buffalo Style: Thick, Cheesy & ‘Roni Cups**


[Buffalo-style pizza](https://www.goldbelly.com/foods/buffalostylepizza) has a soft, fluffy crust and enough cheese to guarantee an epic cheese pull. Its signature topping is pepperoni, but not the wide, flat slices of a New York corner joint. Buffalo’s pepperoni is smaller and cut thicker, so the edges curl into little cups that fill with savory oil as it bakes, known as “cup & char” or “‘roni cups.” Get the real thing from[Picasso’s Pizza](https://www.goldbelly.com/restaurants/picassos-pizza) , a Buffalo icon for more than 40 years, and[La Nova](https://www.goldbelly.com/restaurants/la-nova) .


**The case for it:** ‘Roni cups. Need we say more?


## **Baltimore Style: A Taste of The Chesapeake**


Baltimore may not be the first city that comes to mind as a pizza town, but it has a style all its own. Baltimore pizza has a thick, focaccia-like crust and a whole lot of melty, stretchy cheese.[Matthew’s Pizza](https://www.goldbelly.com/restaurants/matthews-pizza) is the city’s oldest pizzeria, and its signature crab pie is loaded with fresh Maryland crab, a nod to the state’s place on the Chesapeake Bay.


**The case for it:** Crab on pizza. Only in Maryland.


## **Minnesota Style: Thin, Crispy & Party-Cut**


[Minnesota-style pizza](https://www.goldbelly.com/foods/minnesota-style-pizza) is all about a thin, crispy crust with toppings spread right to the edge, cut into squares so everyone at the table can grab a piece. Taste it from Hibbing’s[Sammy’s Pizza](https://www.goldbelly.com/restaurants/sammys-pizza) on the Iron Range and Milaca’s[Heggies Pizza](https://www.goldbelly.com/restaurants/heggies-pizza) , famous for its thin-crust pies in flavors from classic pepperoni to breakfast.


**The case for it:** Party-cut squares were made for sharing, so nobody fights over the last slice.


## **Miami Style: Square Pies in the Sunshine State**


In Miami, the name that comes up first is[Frankie’s Pizza](https://www.goldbelly.com/restaurants/frankies-pizza) , which bills itself as the city’s first pizzeria and is known for its square cheese and pepperoni pies. Explore more[Miami-style pizza](https://www.goldbelly.com/foods/miami-style-pizza) on Goldbelly.


**The case for it:** A homegrown square-pie tradition most pizza fans have never tried.


## **California Style: All About the Toppings**


California-style pizzas are usually single-serving, with a crust similar to New York-style. Where they really stand apart is the toppings. When Wolfgang Puck popularized the style at his West Hollywood hotspot Spago in the 1980s, toppings like goat cheese, duck sausage, smoked salmon, prosciutto, and zucchini flowers were simply unheard of, inspired by the local, seasonal “California cuisine” movement. Order a taste of the original from[Wolfgang Puck](https://www.goldbelly.com/restaurants/wolfgang-puck-catering) .


**The case for it:** It turned pizza into a canvas for fresh, seasonal ingredients.
